newsitem.title: UK: Prince Charles aide out after gaffes over Camilla.
newsitem.headline: Prince Charles aide out after gaffes over Camilla.

text.p: Prince Charles's private secretary was reported on Saturday to have broken down in tears after being sacked for what was seen as public relations gaffes over the prince's relationship with mistress Camilla Parker Bowles.
Richard Aylard, the closest aide of the heir to the British throne, will leave his job early next year after 11 years with the prince. No successor has been named.
Buckingham Palace said Aylard was leaving by mutual decision but the British media said he was shattered after being told he was to be "released."

Aylard, 44, a former naval officer who spearheaded a campaign for more royal openess, is believed to have been behind Charles's confession of adultery with Parker Bowles during an in-depth television documentary in 1994.

He was also blamed for more recent attempts in the press to improve the image of Parker Bowles in a bid to persuade the British public to accept her as Charles's companion following his divorce from Princess Diana.

"The prince had devloped a lack of confidence in Richard. He was also under pressure from other members of the family, including the queen...to confront matters," The Sun newspaper quoted an unidentified royal source as saying.
Charles's popularity has plummeted in the past three years as newspapers revelled in details of his affair with old-flame Parker Bowles.
Diana, who later admitted adultery with cavalry officer James Hewitt, is viewed by most Britons as the wronged party in the 15 year marriage that ended in August.

Prince Charles's biographer Jonathan Dimbleby, who conducted the ground-breaking television documentary, said on Saturday he was unconvinced that Aylard was leaving because of the infidelity admission.
"I think the prince in the end made up his own mind," Dimbleby told BBC radio.

Charles, 47, has said he has no plans to re-marry but the publication last month of a rare photo showing him with Parker Bowles fanned speculation that he might still hold out the hope of formalising his 20-year love affair with Parker-Bowles.
Church leaders are against the idea and opinion polls show Britons are overwhelmingly hostile to the notion of a Queen Camilla.
